# Results — Study 85 (Dr-Copper) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The copper/gold ratio
(HG=F / GC=F) as a predictive signal for forward equity returns (^GSPC) and bond yields
(^TNX). Tested as lagged regression and expanding-window OOS R² against the Goyal-Welch
(2008) naive-mean benchmark. Daily data 2000-08-30 to 2026-06-12 (the overlap of all
four series), weekly and monthly resampling. As-of **2026-06-12**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Rows | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| HG=F  | 2000-08-30 → 2026-06-12 | 6,475 | Copper front-month futures ($/lb) |
| GC=F  | 2000-08-30 → 2026-06-12 | 6,470 | Gold front-month futures ($/troy oz) |
| ^GSPC | 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 6,651 | S&P 500 index |
| ^TNX  | 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 6,645 | 10y US Treasury yield (%) |

**Aligned panel:** 6,493 daily rows (2000-08-30 → 2026-06-12)

Equity (^GSPC close) fingerprint: `8d361abc3a09`

## Weekly regression results

Predictor: copper/gold log-ratio change at week *t*. Target: equity log-return or yield
change at week *t+1* (strictly forward, no look-ahead). Baseline: historical-mean return
(Goyal-Welch benchmark). Sample: **1,344 weekly periods**.

### In-sample

| Target | β | HAC *t* | R² | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fwd equity return** | **−0.044** | **−1.81** | **0.45%** | 1,344 |
| Fwd yield change | −0.032 | −0.29 | 0.01% | 1,344 |
| **Contemporaneous equity** (same week) | **+0.230** | **+6.42** | **12.2%** | 1,344 |

The contemporaneous correlation is strong and correctly signed (ratio up → equities up,
R² = 12.2%, t = 6.4). The predictive regression is **wrong-signed and weak** (β = −0.044,
t = −1.81) — the ratio and equities move together, but the ratio does not *lead* equities.

### Out-of-sample (expanding window, min 52 weeks training)

| Target | OOS R² | DM *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Equity** | **−0.30%** | **−0.60** |
| Yield | −0.59% | −1.11 |

OOS R² is **negative** for both targets — the copper/gold model is outperformed by the
simple historical-mean forecast. The Diebold-Mariano t-stat is insignificant and negative,
confirming no predictive gain.

## Monthly regression results

Sample: **309 monthly periods**.

| Target | β | HAC *t* | R² | OOS R² | DM *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Fwd equity return | +0.061 | +1.17 | 1.04% | −0.02% | −0.01 |
| Fwd yield change | +0.073 | +0.75 | 0.28% | — | — |
| Contemporaneous equity | +0.394 | +6.04 | 7.2% | — | — |

Monthly results confirm the same pattern: contemporaneous R² is substantial (7.2%) but the
predictive regression barely clears t = 1.2 in-sample and the OOS R² is essentially zero.

## The key contrast: contemporaneous vs predictive

| | Contemporaneous | Predictive (weekly, t+1) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **β** | +0.230 | −0.044 |
| **R²** | 12.2% | 0.45% |
| **HAC t** | +6.42 | −1.81 |

The copper/gold ratio has a strong *coincident* relationship with equities — it moves with
the business cycle at the same time. It does not, however, lead equities. The "Dr. Copper
has a PhD" narrative conflates **contemporaneous** correlation (real and robust) with
**predictive** power (absent).

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK/NONE.** IS weekly t = −1.81 (wrong sign!); monthly t = +1.17
  (right sign but < 2); OOS R² negative at both horizons. The inference bar is not cleared.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No reliable directional signal means no tradable edge on
  equity timing. The contemporaneous link is untradable (you'd need to know the ratio
  change and the equity return at the same instant).
- **Contemporaneous/Coincident?** — CONFIRMED. The copper/gold ratio is a legitimate
  coincident indicator (12.2% contemporaneous R²) but fails as a *forecast*.
